name: Istio
summary: A service mesh that separates a Kubernetes-oriented control plane from proxy data planes, distributes traffic and security configuration to workload proxies, and exposes policy-driven routing and telemetry behavior.

features.name: Control-plane distribution to workload proxies
features.description: Istio control-plane components translate mesh configuration and service information into proxy configuration distributed to data-plane proxies.
features.benefits: Centralizes mesh policy while keeping request forwarding near workloads
features.costs: Configuration propagation, proxy compatibility, and stale views add operational coordination cost

features.name: Proxy-mediated traffic management
features.description: Istio workload proxies intercept and forward application traffic, applying routing, load balancing, retries, and other policy configured through mesh APIs.
features.benefits: Adds consistent traffic behavior without changing each application
features.costs: Sidecar resource overhead and policy interactions expand the request path

features.name: Identity, security, and telemetry at mesh boundaries
features.description: Istio associates workload identity with mutual TLS and authorization policy, while proxies emit telemetry that can be configured and collected across mesh traffic.
features.benefits: Provides uniform identity-aware controls and mesh-level observability
features.costs: Certificate lifecycle, policy misconfiguration, and telemetry volume affect reliability and cost

mathematical_views.question: How do service registry observations and mesh configuration reach proxy-local forwarding state?
assumptions: Control-plane objects and discovery responses are modeled as control edges
Each proxy has a local data-plane state that may lag updates
The view does not infer propagation latency or universal consistency

mathematical_views.question: How do services, workloads, proxies, and routing rules determine request paths?
assumptions: Proxies are graph vertices on modeled traffic paths
Traffic policies constrain admissible edges and forwarding choices
The view abstracts Envoy implementation details

mathematical_views.question: Which workload identities and authorization rules permit or deny mesh communication?
assumptions: Workload identity is represented independently from network location
Authorization decisions use configured policy and authenticated peer identity
The view is a candidate correspondence, not a proof of security policy completeness

costs: Control-plane health and config freshness affect data-plane behavior
Proxy hops consume CPU/memory and increase debugging complexity
Certificate, policy, and telemetry systems add lifecycle and operational load
